newsitem.title: USA: Conn. lawmakers seek ban on cancer insurance.
newsitem.headline: Conn. lawmakers seek ban on cancer insurance.

text.p: State Senate leaders said Wednesday they will seek a ban on the sale of cancer insurance and other specialty health policies.
They said they were "extremely disappointed" to learn that the state planned to lift a 21-year ban on selling such policies, starting June 1.
"If we allow this ban to be lifted, there is a real danger in us undermining and fragmenting health insurance in Connecticut," Senate President Pro Tem Kevin Sullivan (D) said in a statement.
He said the policies were often overpriced and did not offer comprehensive coverage.
"These insurance policies are deceptive and do nothing more than play off people's fears," Sullivan said.
He said he expected to receive "strong support" from the House of Representatives on the issue.
"If, over time, the market is allowed to create niche insurance policies by disease, at some point we will likely see a lot of coverages being dropped out," Sullivan said.
"Instead, if you want to be covered for cancer, you'll have to buy cancer insurance. If you want to be covered for heart disease, you'll have to buy heart insurance, and so on."
